title: "Replicating the Measurement Error Simulation in Boulesteix et al. (2020)"
author: "Badr El Jaouhari"
format: pdf
bibliography: references.bib

## Introduction

This document replicates the simulation study of @boulesteix2020, which examines the effect of measurement error in HbA1c and BMI on the estimated association between HbA1c and systolic blood pressure.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| echo: false
library(Hmisc)
library(mice)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: read-data

d1 <- sasxport.get("data/raw/DEMO_I.XPT") 
d2 <- sasxport.get("data/raw/BPX_I.XPT")   
d3 <- sasxport.get("data/raw/BMX_I.XPT")   
d4 <- sasxport.get("data/raw/GHB_I.XPT")   
d5 <- sasxport.get("data/raw/TCHOL_I.XPT") 
d1.t <- subset(d1,select=c("seqn","riagendr","ridageyr"))
d2.t <- subset(d2,select=c("seqn","bpxsy1"))
d3.t <- subset(d3,select=c("seqn","bmxbmi"))
d4.t <- subset(d4,select=c("seqn","lbxgh"))
d5.t <- subset(d5,select=c("seqn","lbdtcsi"))
d <- merge(d1.t,d2.t)
d <- merge(d,d3.t)
d <- merge(d,d4.t)
d <- merge(d,d5.t)
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-data

d$age <- d$ridageyr
d$sex <- d$riagendr
d$bp <- d$bpxsy1
d$bmi <- d$bmxbmi
d$HbA1C <- d$lbxgh
d$chol <- d$lbdtcsi
d$age[d$age<18] <- NA

dc <- cc(subset(d,select=c("age","sex","bmi","HbA1C","bp")))
```

The analysis includes `r nrow(dc)` complete cases.

## Reference models

```{r}
#| label: reference-models
summary(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
confint(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
summary(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
confint(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
```

## Simulation study

The original script adds independent normal measurement errors to HbA1c and BMI, considering 0% to 50% error variance for each variable. There are 36 scenarios, each repeated 1,000 times.

```{r}
#| label: simulation-setup
ref <- lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc)$coef[2]
n.sim <- 1e3
perc.me.exp <- seq(0,.5,.1)
perc.me.conf<- seq(0,.5,.1)
scenarios <- expand.grid(perc.me.exp,perc.me.conf)
var.exp <- var(dc$HbA1C)
var.conf <- var(dc$bmi)
n <- dim(dc)[1]
beta.hat <- matrix(ncol=dim(scenarios)[1], nrow=n.sim)
```

```{r}
#| label: simulation-loop
#| results: hide
for (k in 1:n.sim){
  print(k)
  set.seed(k)
  for (i in 1:dim(scenarios)[1]){
    var.me.exp <- var.exp*scenarios[i,1]/(1-scenarios[i,1])
    var.me.conf <- var.conf*scenarios[i,2]/(1-scenarios[i,2])
    dc$HbA1C.me <- dc$HbA1C + rnorm(dim(dc)[1], 0, sqrt(var.me.exp) )
    dc$bmi.me <- dc$bmi + rnorm(dim(dc)[1], 0, sqrt(var.me.conf) )
    beta.hat[k,i] <- lm(bp ~ HbA1C.me + age + bmi.me + as.factor(sex), data=dc)$coef[2]
  }}
```

## Results

```{r}
#| label: figure
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Mean HbA1c coefficients for each measurement-error scenario."
tot.mat <- cbind(100*scenarios,apply(beta.hat,2,mean))
colnames(tot.mat) <- c("me.exp","me.conf","estimate")
tot.mat <- as.data.frame(tot.mat) # Added this line to make ggplot2 work with a data-frame object not a matrix
FIGURE <- ggplot(tot.mat, aes(me.exp, me.conf)) +
  geom_tile(color="white",aes(fill = estimate)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2))) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="#D55E00",mid="white",high = "#56B4E9", midpoint=ref) +
  labs(x=paste("% of total variance of HbA1c due to measurement error"),
       y=paste("% of total variance of BMI due to measurement error")) +
  coord_equal()+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=unique(tot.mat[,1]))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(tot.mat[,1]))+
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill='white', colour='grey'),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust=0),
        axis.ticks=element_blank(),
        axis.title=element_text(size=12),
        axis.text=element_text(size=10),
        legend.title=element_text(size=12),
        legend.text=element_text(size=10))
FIGURE
```

The heatmap shows that when measurement error is added to HbA1c, its estimated coefficient decreases from 0.75 to 0.35, weakening the estimated association with systolic blood pressure. In contrast, error in BMI increases the coefficient to 0.94 because it makes the adjustment for confounding less effective. When both variables contain error, these effects partly cancel out. The results show that measurement error can either decrease or increase the estimated association between HbA1c and systolic blood pressure, depending on which variable is affected.
